title: Street control rumours and the 1963 attempt to bring a band back
summary: Places are individually owned; Sid tried Bill Matthews' band in 1963.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I see. Is there any, is there much sort of, uh, do you sense that there's much sort of pressure on the street to try and perform or to produce entertainment in a certain style or anything like that? No, I don't think so. I'm always hearing, you know, you always hear these stories about the places that are being controlled by a few people and so on, and I was wondering if you had been subjected to any of these pressures or anything like that?

No, that's not, that's not true at all. These places are individually owned, and, uh, and actually, if someone would come in and, uh, not a syndicate, but an organization, which we attempted to do several times, try to, uh, put some uniformity on the street, such as prices and hours and, uh, cutthroat activities, crit to your left. I think we'd all benefit. But, uh, it's not the case. They're individually owned by guys that don't have too much money. And it's kind of a hit of scare them, catch as catch can, you know? Yes.
It's almost. Is that right? You really think that, in other words, there isn't that much uniformity on the street, do you?
